{"self_assessment": "Impact: I proposed the fish at the start of the round: a big body, nose on the left, forked tail on the right. It is a simple outline that a judge can read quickly, and the table adopted it right away. I built the upper tail lobe, which branches off the top line. That lobe gives the fork its upper half, so it is one of the features that makes the outline read as a fish. At the push, the run was connected across all 115 standing dominoes.

Execution: I traced the upper tail lobe from the pad in a series of builds. It joined the main line cleanly and had no breaks. I then inspected the lobe and its join near the start three separate times (at about 3:30, 4:30 and 5:00) and confirmed it was connected. Once everything was down, I kept my hands off the table so nothing could be bumped before the push.

Collaboration: I kept the table informed throughout, with short updates on what I was building and how it was going. I helped settle who took which stroke, and I offered to take the far end of the lower lobe if Leo needed help. I stayed out of other people's areas to avoid bumps, and I gave quick feedback as the lines reached each other.

Leadership: I set the direction early by choosing the animal and the layout. I got the table moving by proposing a split of the work: top line, bottom line and the two tail lobes. I kept the pace up with regular check-ins and made sure the picture was verified from start to both tail tips before time ran out. I also chose to hold back at the end rather than risk disturbing a finished build.", "my_share_percent": 30}
